edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Longer breastfeeding may strengthen early satiety signaling and reduce ultra-processed exposure in infancy, a plausible route to lower later obesity risk.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2025 Liu meta analysis in BMC Womens Health already points to breastfeeding for at least 6 months tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
